explanation: PEMDAS says multiplication happens before addition, so a + b×c means a + (b×c), not (a+b)×c. Move the a, b, and c sliders and step through the worked solution: the highlighted box shows which operation is done first, and the right-hand column shows the wrong answer you get if you ignore the rule. The bottom readout always reports the correct value a + b×c.
bullets: Multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction.
Grouping with parentheses can override the default order.
a + b×c ≠ (a+b)×c whenever b×c and (a+b)×c differ.
